entities.summary:
Xiahou Ba (courtesy name Zhongquan, died 262 CE) was a pivotal figure in the late Cao Wei and early Shu Han states during China's Three Kingdoms period, whose defection from Wei to Shu in 249 CE dramatically underscored the internal political turmoil engulfing Cao Wei and the consolidation of power by the Sima clan. As the second son of the prominent Cao Wei general Xiahou Yuan and a nephew of Cao Cao's wife, Lady Ding, Xiahou Ba initially held significant military positions within Wei, commanding forces along the border with Shu Han. His strategic shift highlighted the deep factionalism and mistrust that permeated the Wei court following the death of Emperor Cao Rui and the subsequent power struggles between the regents Cao Shuang and Sima Yi.

The core event defining Xiahou Ba's career was his decision to abandon Cao Wei after Sima Yi's successful coup d'état at the Gaoping Tombs in 249 CE, which effectively seized control from Cao Shuang and his faction. Fearing retribution due to his familial ties to the Cao clan and his association with Cao Shuang, Xiahou Ba fled westward, navigating treacherous terrain to defect to Wei's rival state, Shu Han. His arrival was celebrated by Shu's regent, Jiang Wei, who saw in Xiahou Ba not only a respected general but also a potent symbol of Wei's internal disunity, granting him the title of General of the Left and Marquis of Anguo and frequently consulting him on campaigns against Wei, particularly during Jiang Wei's northern expeditions.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Xiahou Ba's defection was a significant event that both reflected and influenced the power dynamics of the Three Kingdoms, bolstering Shu Han's military and symbolizing the political instability within Cao Wei following the Sima clan's rise. His actions provided valuable intelligence and legitimacy to Shu Han's campaigns against Wei.
